nodes.question: What has been the average decline in the abundance of freshwater populations according to the Freshwater Living Planet Index from 1970 to 2016?
nodes.answer: The average decline in the abundance of freshwater populations is 76% from 1970 to 2016.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are the implications of high nutrient availability in the Ebro Delta area?
nodes.answer: High nutrient availability contributes to a favorable environment for fish nursery, supports high biodiversity, and includes species of commercial interest.
nodes.paragraph: 2014; Bevilacqua et al. 2019; Chakravorty et al. 2024). Materials and methods Study area The study area is the surroundings of the Ebro Delta, in the Northwestern Mediterranean Sea, from Vilanova i la Geltr , in the north, to Castell de la Plana, in the south, covering approximately 8,0 km2 and including part of the coastal area, continental shelf, and upper slope (35 400 m) (Fig. 1). Despite that the Mediterranean Sea is generally considered oligotrophic, this area receives high riverine inputs from the Ebro river (Estrada 1996) and from the Rhone River in the north (France), which are transported southwestwards along the continental slope by the Liguro-Proven al-Catalan cur - rent (Estrada 1996). In addition, local upwelling events (i.e., eddies) also enhance nutrient availability. The area is also characterized by strong seasonality (Vilas et al. 2020; Lloret- Lloret et al. 2021). Overall, the wide continental shelf sur - rounding the Ebro Delta, combined with high nutrient avail- ability, upwelling events, and seasonal dynamics, contributes to create a favourable environment for fish nursery for many demersal and pelagic species that also supports high biodi- versity and high biomass, including species of commercial interest (Palomera et al.
